title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Chapter 6: Following the Cash — 10-Year Financials & Earnings Quality

epigraph.quote: Revenue is vanity, profit is sanity, but cash conversion and clean balance sheets are reality.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.html: Anand Rathi Wealth's 10-year financial trajectory (FY16–FY26 plus Sep 2026 TTM) exhibits textbook asset-light compounding [1]. Consolidated sales scaled from Rs 214 Cr in FY18 (standalone) and Rs 280 Cr in FY19 to Rs 1,253 Cr in FY26—a 5-year profit CAGR of 54.7% from the FY21 COVID trough (Rs 45 Cr) to FY26 (Rs 397 Cr) [1]. Operating margins expanded from 33%–36% pre-IPO to 43%–47% across FY22–FY26 as RM productivity doubled [1].

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year Consolidated Profit & Loss Statement (Rs Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Sales compounded from Rs 280 Cr (FY19) to Rs 1,253 Cr (FY26) with OPM expanding to 47%, while TTM (Sep 2026) reflects ESOP-2025 expense compression (36% OPM) offset by Rs 207 Cr Other Income.

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year Consolidated Balance Sheet (Rs Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Virtually debt-free (Rs 69 Cr borrowings vs Rs 1,283 Cr equity + reserves in Sep 2026); note the rapid expansion in Other Assets (Rs 530 Cr -> Rs 873 Cr -> Rs 1,070 Cr) and Investments (Rs 112 Cr -> Rs 358 Cr).

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year Consolidated Cash Flow & Free Cash Flow (Rs Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Cumulative FY22–FY26 CFO of Rs 1,032 Cr against Rs 1,220 Cr cumulative PAT (~85% CFO/PAT conversion), with minimal capex enabling Rs 948 Cr of cumulative Free Cash Flow.

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year Working Capital & Return Ratios
web_blocks.takeaway: ROCE climbed steadily from 49% (FY22) to 59% (FY26), while Debtor Days remained tight at 11–14 days.

web_blocks.html:
Forensic Deep-Dive — Three Critical Balance-Sheet & P&L Signals:
1. The TTM Other Income Spike (Rs 207 Cr) & ESOP Offset: Across FY22–FY26, annual Other Income was tiny at Rs 0–1 Cr/year [1]. In Q4 FY26 (Rs 68 Cr) and Q1 FY27 (Rs 110 Cr), Other Income jumped to Rs 207 Cr TTM. This came from mark-to-market fair-value gains on treasury and group investments, such as holdings in Anand Rathi Global Finance [1][6]. Meanwhile, ARWL ESOP-2025 non-cash charges lifted Expenses from Rs 158–160 Cr/quarter to Rs 203–227 Cr/quarter. That compressed headline OPM from 47% (FY26) to 29%–34% in Mar–Sep 2026 [1][10]. Strip out both fair-value gains and front-loaded ESOP noise to see core operating cash earnings.
2. Working Capital & Other Assets Expansion: Debtor Days sit at a crisp 12 days. Yet Working Capital Days rose from 26 days (FY22) to 121 days (FY26) as Other Assets climbed from Rs 253 Cr to Rs 873 Cr, reaching Rs 1,070 Cr in Sep 2026 [1]. This reflects growing treasury deployments, security deposits, and accrued receivables. It also explains why FY26 CFO (Rs 281 Cr) trailed PAT (Rs 397 Cr) at 70% CFO/EBITDA [1].
3. Capital Allocation & Shareholder Returns: Equity + Reserves reached Rs 1,283 Cr (Sep 2026) against just Rs 69 Cr of borrowings. ARWL earns 47.3% ROE and 59.2% ROCE while maintaining a 27%–39% dividend payout, plus a 1:1 bonus and buybacks in FY25 [1][21].

web_blocks.title: Forensic Verdict on Earnings Quality
paragraphs: Core FY22–FY26 cash conversion (~85% cumulative CFO/PAT, Rs 948 Cr cumulative FCF) confirms that historical earnings are overwhelmingly real cash, not accounting accruals [1].

Going forward, the key forensic watch item is ensuring that the Rs 207 Cr TTM Other Income fair-value gains are never treated as recurring operating earnings, and that rising Other Assets (Rs 1,070 Cr) remain liquid, arm's-length treasury assets rather than related-party working capital.

book_paragraphs: Numbers never lie, provided you know which footnotes to read. When you and I open Anand Rathi Wealth's ten-year financial ledger, the first impression is breathtaking: revenue marches from Rs 280 crore in FY19 to Rs 1,253 crore in FY26. Net profit leaps from Rs 58 crore to Rs 397 crore. Return on Capital Employed sits at a jaw-dropping 59.2%, and Return on Equity is 47.3%. The company carries almost zero debt—just Rs 69 crore of lease/short-term liabilities against Rs 1,283 crore of equity and reserves.

Now let's put on our forensic-auditor hat and ask the uncomfortable questions. First, look at Other Income. For five straight years from FY22 to FY26, annual Other Income was basically zero—Rs 0 to Rs 1 crore a year. Then suddenly, in March 2026 it jumped to Rs 68 crore, in June 2026 it hit Rs 110 crore, and on a trailing twelve-month basis it sits at Rs 207 crore! At the exact same time, Operating Profit Margins dropped from 47% in FY26 to 29%–34% in the last three quarters. What happened? Two accounting distortions collided: front-loaded non-cash ESOP charges under ARWL ESOP-2025 pushed employee expenses up, while mark-to-market fair-value gains on treasury investments inflated Other Income. Never extrapolate Rs 207 crore of fair-value gains as permanent operating profit.

Second, look at Cash Flow from Operations. Over the five-year stretch from FY22 to FY26, ARWL generated Rs 1,032 crore of operating cash flow against Rs 1,220 crore of net profit—an impressive 85% cash conversion ratio—and spent only Rs 84 crore on capex, yielding Rs 948 crore of Free Cash Flow. Yet in FY26 alone, CFO was Rs 281 crore against Rs 397 crore of PAT (70% CFO/EBITDA). Why? Because 'Other Assets' swelled from Rs 530 crore to Rs 873 crore in FY26 and Rs 1,070 crore by September 2026, lifting Working Capital Days to 121 days. As long as those Other Assets are liquid treasury instruments and short-term receivables (Debtor Days are still just 12 days), the cash engine is sound—but it is a line item you should check every six months.

With Pass 1 complete, our price-blind verdict is clear: Anand Rathi Wealth earns a COMPOUNDER_PASS on business quality with a kpi_health rating of PASS_WITH_WATCH—an exceptional, asset-light wealth compounder whose only real vulnerabilities are its 28% structured-product/ARGFL concentration, ESOP/fair-value P&L noise, and gradual promoter dilution.

book_callouts.title: Narrator's Reflection: Separating Core Cash from Accounting Noise
paragraphs: When ESOP accounting charges depress reported operating margins and fair-value gains inflate Other Income in the same year, casual readers get confused.
Focus on three anchors: (1) core adjusted revenue growth (~17%–22%), (2) net inflows (>Rs 6,900 Cr in H1 FY27), and (3) multi-year cumulative Free Cash Flow (Rs 948 Cr over FY22–FY26).
